statements.text: Right lower back strain after lifting a box of floor tile on Saturday.

evidence.quote: Saturday I was helping move pallets at work, and I picked up a box of floor tile wrong.

statements.text: Current pain 6/10, 8/10 with bending over.

evidence.quote: Right now, maybe a 6. When I bend over to tie my shoes, it's like an 8.

statements.text: Radiates a little into the right buttock, not down the leg.

evidence.quote: A little into the right butt cheek. Not down the leg.

statements.text: Denies leg or foot numbness, tingling, or weakness.

evidence.quote: Any numbness or tingling in your legs or feet? Any weakness, like your foot dragging?
No, no numbness. Legs feel normal, just the back.

statements.text: Denies saddle-area numbness.

evidence.quote: Any numbness in the groin or between your legs, like where you'd sit on a saddle?
No.

statements.text: Denies bladder or bowel dysfunction.

evidence.quote: Any trouble controlling your bladder or bowels, or trouble starting to pee?
No, everything's working fine there.

statements.text: Denies fever, unexplained weight loss, or history of cancer.

evidence.quote: Any fevers, unexplained weight loss, or any history of cancer?
None of that.

statements.text: History of left-sided sciatica six years ago, treated with physical therapy, resolved.

evidence.quote: Have you had back trouble before?
I had sciatica on the left side maybe six years ago. Did physical therapy and it went away completely, haven't had it since.

statements.text: Self-treated with ibuprofen and heat; works, but worries about disc herniation given coworker's experience.

evidence.quote: Ibuprofen, two of the 200s a couple times a day, and my wife's heating pad. The heat helps some. I'm kind of worried, though.

statements.text: Works as a shift lead in a warehouse at Harbor Point Distribution.

evidence.quote: Where do you work again?
Harbor Point Distribution. I'm a shift lead in the warehouse.

statements.text: Vital signs: blood pressure 134/84, pulse 76, temperature 98.4.

evidence.quote: Blood pressure is 134 over 84, pulse 76, temperature 98.4.

statements.text: Forward bending limited by pain to about halfway.

evidence.quote: Can you stand and bend forward for me?
That's about as far as I go.
forward bending is limited by pain, about halfway.

statements.text: Tender, tight muscles along the right lower back; no spinous process tenderness.

evidence.quote: I can feel tight, tender muscles along the right side of your lower back. No tenderness when I press right on the spine itself.

statements.text: Straight leg raise negative bilaterally.

evidence.quote: Now lie back. I'm going to raise each leg straight.
Straight leg raise is negative on both sides.

statements.text: Motor strength normal in both legs; reflexes equal at knees and ankles; sensation intact bilaterally.

evidence.quote: Strength is normal in both legs, reflexes are equal at the knees and ankles, and you can feel my touch the same on both sides.

statements.text: Walked in normally and could walk on heels and toes.

evidence.quote: You walked in normally, and you can walk on your heels and toes.

statements.text: Acute musculoskeletal strain of the lower back muscles.

evidence.quote: This looks like a strain of the muscles in your lower back.

statements.text: No indication for X-ray or MRI at this time; no neurologic red flags.

evidence.quote: There are no warning signs, so you don't need an X-ray or MRI right now.

statements.text: Expected recovery in 2 to 4 weeks.

evidence.quote: Most of these get a lot better in 2 to 4 weeks.

flags.message: Quoted turn does not contain most of its terms; check against the transcript.

statements.text: Ibuprofen 600 mg taken three times daily with food for about one week.

evidence.quote: take ibuprofen 600 milligrams three times a day with food for the next week or so.

statements.text: Cyclobenzaprine 5 mg at bedtime as needed for spasm; can cause drowsiness.

evidence.quote: I'm also prescribing cyclobenzaprine, a muscle relaxer, 5 milligrams at bedtime as needed for spasm.

statements.text: Precaution: no driving or operating the forklift after taking cyclobenzaprine.

evidence.quote: It can make you drowsy, so no driving or running the forklift after you take it.

statements.text: Continue heat application and stay active; gentle walking preferred over bed rest.

evidence.quote: Keep using heat, and keep moving. Gentle walking is better than bed rest.

statements.text: Light-duty work note issued, no lifting over 20 pounds, valid through October 15th.

evidence.quote: I'll write you a note for light duty, no lifting over 20 pounds, through October 15th.

statements.text: Return for evaluation in 2 weeks; physical therapy will be started if not better in 2 weeks.

evidence.quote: If you're not better in 2 weeks, come back and we'll start physical therapy.
Let's plan a follow-up in 2 weeks.

statements.text: Emergency return precautions: loss of bladder or bowel control, numbness between the legs, or leg weakness.

evidence.quote: And if you ever lose control of your bladder or bowels, get numb between your legs, or a leg gets weak, go to the emergency room right away.
take ibuprofen 600 milligrams three times a day with food for the next week or so.
I'm also prescribing cyclobenzaprine, a muscle relaxer, 5 milligrams at bedtime as needed for spasm.

note.after_visit_summary:
You hurt your lower back after lifting a box of floor tile at work. You have a muscle strain, not a bad back injury. No x-ray or MRI is needed. This should get much better in 2 to 4 weeks.

Take ibuprofen 600 mg by mouth three times a day with food for about one week. Take cyclobenzaprine 5 mg at night only if you have muscle spasms. It can make you sleepy, so do not drive or run the forklift after taking it.

Use heat on your back and keep moving. Walk gently instead of resting in bed. I have given you a note for light duty at work with no lifting over 20 pounds until October 15th.

Come back in 2 weeks, or go to the emergency room right away if you lose control of your bladder or bowels, get numb between your legs, or your leg gets weak. Hopefully, you will be feeling much better soon.
